customManagers.description: TF_VERSION in the Terraform workflows (both files move in one PR). The provider lock does not depend on the Terraform version, but read the release notes before merging: the plan after merge must still show no changes.
PACKER_VERSION in the Packer template workflow.

Host OTel agent (monitoring_stack/splunk/otel-agent/install.sh). SHA256 sits beside VERSION and a regex manager can't compute it, so this waits for Dependency Dashboard approval: see the packageRule for host pins with a checksum.

Host Falco (monitoring_stack/falco/install.sh). Installed from Falco's GPG-signed apt repository as falco=<VERSION>, so a version-only PR is complete. Merging changes nothing until install.sh is re-run on each host.
kube-bench on k3s-01 (kube_bench/install.sh). SHA256 sits beside VERSION, so this waits for Dependency Dashboard approval.

k3s on k3s-01 (k3s_node/k3s-version). K3S_SHA256 sits beside it, and upgrade-k3s.sh is run by hand: patch releases within the running minor only, on Dependency Dashboard approval. Release candidates don't match the versioning regex, so they're ignored.

packageRules.description: gha-runner-scale-set must match the ARC controller version (arc-controller-k3s, pinned in its ArgoCD app, which Renovate can't see). Upgrade controller and scale sets together by hand.

The ToolHive CRDs chart (toolhive_crds) must move in lockstep with the operator chart (toolhive_operator): one PR for both. Read the release notes for CRD changes before merging: see Upgrading ToolHive in infrastructure_tooling/toolhive_mcp/README.md. OCI charts are named by their full registry path, so short chart names don't match.

The tailscale-operator chart is vendored under charts/ (a bare Chart.yaml bump is a no-op that desyncs Chart.lock), and it is applied to docker-compose-03 by hand, not by Argo CD. Upgrade by hand: see the Tailscale Kubernetes Operator section of docs/secondary-cluster.md.

Argo CD itself (infrastructure_tooling/argocd) is applied by hand, so merging a bump changes nothing until someone applies it, and each release only supports certain Kubernetes versions. Upgrade by hand: see infrastructure_tooling/argocd/README.md.
Charts are vendored under charts/: have Renovate run helm dependency update so a chart bump commits the new tgz too (otherwise the old one keeps rendering).

Everything in the homelab agents image (Python lock and both Chainguard digests, which must move together) rebuilds the same :main image the CronJobs run: one PR, one rebuild. requirements.txt is a uv pip compile lock that Renovate edits pin by pin (its pip-compile manager can't take --python-platform), so if the build fails, re-run the uv pip compile command in its header on the PR branch.

The mcp-for-argocd image (infrastructure_tooling/mcp_for_argocd_image): both Chainguard Node digests build the same image, so they move in one PR, and the image must be rebuilt and its new digest pinned in toolhive_mcp values (mcpServers.argocd) after merge.

pydantic pins pydantic-core to one exact version, so pydantic-core only moves when pydantic does (re-locking with the uv pip compile command in requirements.txt picks it up). Renovate bumped it on its own once (#295), to a version pydantic couldn't use and with no Python 3.14 wheel, and the image build failed.

Authentik's database (infrastructure_tooling/authentik): a new Postgres major can't open the old data directory (and 18 moved the image's data path), so a major bump would break the Authentik login for Splunk and Cribl. Patch and minor updates within the major still come through. Move majors by hand with a dump and restore.

Authentik's chart and server image (infrastructure_tooling/authentik) move in one PR, so new chart templates never run with an old image. The image is pinned as tag@digest in global.image.tag; a bare digest: key is invisible to Renovate and would stay on the old image.

kubectl must stay within one minor version of the cluster (k3s-01 runs 1.36): the art-validation runner uses it against the API server. Patch updates up to 1.36 still come through; raise this with the k3s upgrade.
Argo CD Applications that sync a directory of this repo (targetRevision HEAD) have no version to track; their charts and images are tracked through Chart.yaml and values.yaml instead.

Upstream charts pinned in Argo CD Applications (cert-manager, External Secrets, Vault). There is no app-of-apps, so merging a bump does nothing until the application.yaml is applied (and synced, for ESO and Vault): read the upgrade notes at the top of each file first. Majors wait for Dependency Dashboard approval.
cert-manager upgrades one minor version at a time (see cert_manager/application.yaml), so each minor gets its own PR instead of one jumping straight to the newest.

Host pins with a hard-coded SHA-256 beside the version (OTel host agent, kube-bench, k3s). Renovate can only change the version, and the installers fail closed on a hash mismatch, so a PR on its own can't be merged. Approve it on the Dependency Dashboard when you are ready to upgrade, then push the new hash to the PR branch before merging: the steps are next to each pin.
k3s moves one minor at a time by hand with upgrade-k3s.sh (see k3s_node/README.md), and other pins (kubectl) are capped to the running minor. Only patch releases of the running minor are offered.
Chainguard rebuilds its latest images about daily, so each digest would otherwise open a new PR right after the last one merges. Check them weekly, Mondays before 06:00 UTC.
